Render one frame of a keyframe animation

Source: R/animate.R
vl_render_frame.Rd

vl_render_frame() draws the single frame that vl_render_animation() would draw for one schedule entry – keyframe pair seg at fraction frac – and writes it as a still image: a poster for an animation, a thumbnail, or the frame to put in print. The marks are matched and tweened exactly as in the animation (see Matching marks by identity in vl_render_animation()), and a per-frame text variant is swapped in the same way.

Usage

vl_render_frame(
  keyframes,
  seg,
  frac,
  path,
  frac_col = frac,
  frac_size = frac,
  frac_alpha = frac,
  text_variant = NULL,
  text = c("native", "outline"),
  scale = 1
)

Arguments

keyframes

A list of at least two scenes (each a vl_scene() or anything with an as_vellum_scene() method), all the same pixel size.

seg

The 1-based index of the left keyframe of the pair (a single integer in 1:(length(keyframes) - 1)).

frac

The positional fraction between keyframe seg and seg + 1 (a single number; 0 is keyframe seg, 1 is keyframe seg + 1).

path

Output file path; the format is taken from the extension (.png, .svg or .pdf), as for render().

frac_col, frac_size, frac_alpha

The fractions of the other property classes; default frac.

text_variant

A scene whose keyed text replaces the frame's text with the same keys (one entry of text_variants in vl_render_animation()), or NULL.

text

For SVG and PowerPoint output, how text is written: "native" (default) emits selectable, editable text referencing system fonts, "outline" emits glyph outlines (pixel-faithful, identical to the raster/PDF backends, but not selectable). Ignored for PNG/PDF.

scale

Resolution multiplier (default 1). scale = 2 renders at twice the device pixels while keeping the same physical size — the retina / ggsave(scaling=) idiom. It multiplies dpi, so absolute units (mm, pt, in) cover proportionally more pixels and nothing about the layout changes; text does not get relatively bigger or smaller. Only raster output gains anything: a PDF's page size in points and an SVG's physical size are unchanged by construction.

Value

path, invisibly.

See also

vl_render_animation(), render()

Examples

a <- vl_scene(2, 2) |> draw(circle_grob(r = 0.1, gp = vl_gpar(fill = "tomato")))
b <- vl_scene(2, 2) |> draw(circle_grob(r = 0.4, gp = vl_gpar(fill = "tomato")))
vl_render_frame(list(a, b), 1, 0.5, tempfile(fileext = ".png"))
